newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 index penned in, but AVH to gain.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 index penned in, but AVH to gain.

text.p: Brussels' Bel-20 share index quietly nudged into the black on Monday with Belgian blue chips stuck in consolidatory mode, dealers said.

But shares in Ackermans & van Haaren were expected to resume trade after Monday's one-day suspension with solid gains after the holding company announced a capital gain from the merger of a unit with U.S. Pride Petroleum Services Inc.

The Bel-20 rose 1.94 points to 1,812.01 with a moderate 1.3 billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded. The bourse drew little support from a Dow Jones gain .DJI of almost 20 points, but also suffered little pressure from weakish bonds.

The impact of a one-day strike by socialist unions was limited in view of autumn school holidays. Also, christian unions did not take part in the action seeking to maximise pay deals within tight government-imposed ranges.
Dealers said they did not expect much major movement in this week. The only major U.S. indicator -- October jobs data -- is due on Friday when the Belgian share market for All Saints.

Belgian analysts have turned more cautious on the Bel-20, foreseeing little upside scope in the near term as momentum slowed. A steady dollar and relatively low interest rates should, however, mean support at 1,800 points would hold.

The only news of interest to the market was holding AVH's announcement that its Forasol-Foramer NV unit was due to merge with Pride, a Houston-based provider of contract drilling and plugging and abandonment services.
Forasol shareholders can swap one Forasol share for 0.66 Pride share plus $6.80 in cash.
Forasol, quoted in New York, was up $2-3/8 at $16-1/8. With Pride up $5/8 at $15-7/8, the offer values Forasol at $17.28.
AVH said it would obtain 1.07 billion francs in cash plus a stake of 7.2 percent in Pride. It expected to make consolidated capital gain of about 1.0 billion francs on the deal.
One analyst noted every one dollar gain by Forasol should result in a 50 franc increase in AVH shares, so that AVH should now be quoted at at least 4,950 francs.
He said that even after the merger AVH would remain invested in a sector heading for an upswing. Forasol should break even in 1996 before posting a one to $1.1 per share profit in 1997.
"Many players have not discounted that yet, maybe they will once they look at the share again after this news," he added.
PetroFina, a major component in the Bel-20, lost 90 francs at 9,710 after news late on Friday of disappointing third quarter results from Fina, its U.S. unit.
Analyst Patrick Millecam at Corluy said the share was relatively expensive in an international context.

Noting PetroFina was typically a downstream operator, he said that margins in refining remained under pressure as a result of high oil prices. "80 percent of what PetroFina processes it has to buy externally," he noted. Scope for the share to move in either direction was seen limited.
